activities.anchor: do the first and cheapest work
activities.caption: file the heat-island facts — loop or countermeasure?
activities.name: spHeatBuckets

config.prompt: The urban heat island is a feedback loop — file each fact:

items.label: dark, dry, low-albedo surfaces running several degrees warmer
air-conditioning demand rising, pushing ambient heat up again
high-albedo and permeable surfaces, water bodies

config.why: The same physics read generously gives the countermeasures — and vernacular architecture is the discipline's centuries-long dataset on the dynamic.

activities.anchor: demand-side abatement is the cheapest energy in the transition
activities.caption: rebuild the passive-first triad
activities.name: spTriadOrder

config.prompt: Each stage shrinks what the next must do. Order the hierarchy:
items: Passive design: orientation, compact form, envelope, shading, thermal mass
Efficient systems: serve the reduced demand well
Renewable supply: cover what is left
Panels on a leaky building spend their whole output fighting the envelope
The same panels on a Passivhaus-grade building can cover all of its demand
config.why: The Bullitt Center's net-zero depends on the fabric first — and envelope-plus-equipment measures cut demand by half to three-quarters at lower cost per tonne than generation.

config.q: A client proposes solar panels on a leaky 1970s envelope and calls the building sustainable. What is the expert's first move?
choices: Fix the audit order: reduce demand passively, supply efficiently, generate last — the fabric upgrade is usually the cheap part whole-life
Add more panels until the demand is met
Swap the panels for heat pumps and stop there
config.why: Panels are the LAST step of the triad, and on a poor envelope they are the most expensive way to buy comfort — the Passivhaus arithmetic proves near-zero heating demand with no generation device on site.

activities.anchor: insisting, on site, that it was
activities.caption: fill the blanks — closing the performance gap
activities.name: spGapCloze

config.text: Buildings in use routinely consume %%0%% times their models' predictions. The countermeasures: thermal-bridge-free detailing (a repeating junction can add %%1%% per cent to heating demand), blower-door and thermographic %%2%% as quality gates, and commissioning as a deliverable.
config.hint: The gap's range, the junction penalty, and what runs before handover.

activities.caption: pair each embodied-carbon lever with its move
activities.name: spEmbodiedMatch

config.prompt: The levers, in order of power:

pairs.right: adaptive reuse — the greenest building is usually the one already standing
structural efficiency: less material per carried load
mass timber sequesters roughly a tonne of carbon per tonne of wood
EPDs make carbon a selectable attribute — RIBA 2030, LETI targets

config.why: Two equivalent floors — post-tensioned concrete vs timber — differ by tens of kgCO₂e/m² BEFORE either building operates.

activities.anchor: a 60-year asset under a moving hazard map
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the retrofit's demand cut
activities.name: spRetrofitEstimate

config.prompt: Europe's residential stock averages about 190 kWh/m² per year; Passivhaus-grade renovation approaches 15. Roughly what per cent of typical demand does that represent?
config.why: 15 ÷ 190 ≈ 8% — deep-retrofit targets reach 60–80, and the replicated two-thirds-plus demand cut is among the largest single climate levers any profession owns.
config.context: Around 80% of the buildings that will exist in 2050 are already standing — hence retrofit-first.

activities.anchor: working with walls that already exist
activities.caption: bet first — retrofit vs tear-down
activities.name: spRazePredict

config.q: Why does a deep retrofit usually beat a tear-down rebuild on total emissions?
choices: Demolition spends decades of embodied carbon up front — a debt the new building needs half a century or more to repay
New buildings are always leakier than old ones
config.why: Carl Elefante's phrase — 'the greenest building is the one that is already built' — captures the arithmetic; with 80% of 2050's stock already standing, retrofit-first is the governing hierarchy.
